name: ley lines

attributes.attribute: a modern idea with no old Celtic proof
named the old straight line in 1925

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ley lines are a modern belief about hidden lines of power. Some say these lines of earth energy join sacred old sites. The idea began with the British writer Alfred Watkins in 1925. He called his finding the old straight line. No old Celtic text or tale supports this claim. The places they show to connect differ widely in time. The spots also lie far apart in region. Few real straight tracks can be traced on the ground. So the notion has no basis in old Celtic thought.

okr.objective: Show that ley lines are a modern claim rather than old lore.
key_results: The belief is modern, not ancient.
Watkins framed the idea in 1925 in a work.
No ancient Celtic source records such a notion.
The linked sites differ too much in age and place to show lines.
